title: Microsoft Copilot: Excel Agent builds charts, summaries and formulas from your data
summary: Hold: the summary incorrectly turns availability without a Copilot licence into no licence requirement at all. The mixed licensing classification is not documented, and the low cost rating conflicts with the page's own licence-cost premise. The documented control paths and Graph block call check out.

claims.where: Cost and licensing; Open questions: meter; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The feature's Learn page publishes no meter, credit rate or price, and no specific Copilot Credits charge for Excel Agent was found.
claims.quote: Searched: 'Excel Agent Word Excel PowerPoint Agents licensing pricing Copilot Credits meter'; 'Excel Agent billing Credits'. Opened wordexcelppt-agents, usage-based-billing-manage-copilot-credits and usage-based-billing-overview-copilot-credits. No Excel Agent meter or rate found.

claims.where: front matter: cost; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: A low, indirect-cost-only rating is consistent with treating a paid licence for each required user as the main cost.
claims.quote: cost: "low"; 'The indirect costs are the licence for each user who needs the agent and admin time'; 'the main cost is licence and admin time'. The schema defines low as indirect cost only, and medium as add-on licences for a subset of users.
claims.fix: Set cost to 'medium'. Replace the rationale with 'Medium. Budgeting on Learn's stricter entitlement statement may require paid Microsoft 365 Copilot licences for users who lack them; the roadmap reports wider entitlement, and no separate agent meter is published.' Replace 'The indirect costs are the licence for each user who needs the agent and admin time to review the Anthropic setting' with 'The potential direct cost is a paid Microsoft 365 Copilot licence for users who lack one; reviewing the Anthropic setting adds admin time.'
